rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those invoked besides God are the idols and rivals the polytheists worship.
rows.anchor: أي ما تعبدون من الأصنام والأنداد من دون الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge asks whether the idols created anything at all from the earth.
rows.anchor: أي هل خلقوا شيئا من الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shirk here means a share in creating the heavens alongside God.
rows.anchor: أي نصيب { في السماوات } أي في خلق السموات مع الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requested earlier book would be one that came before this Qur'an.
rows.anchor: أي من قبل هذا القرآن.

rows.speaker: قراءة العامة
rows.claim: The common reading is athārah, with an alif after the thāʾ.
rows.anchor: «أو أثارة» بألف بعد الثاء.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن النبي
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet explained athārah as lines Arabs used to trace on the ground.
rows.anchor: هو خط كانت تخطه العرب في الأرض

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi judged the Ibn Abbas report about geomantic lines unsound.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن العربي: ولم يصح.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the line report is established through Muawiya ibn al-Hakam in Muslim and gives another sound route from Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: قلت: هو ثابت من حديث معاوية بن الحكم السلمي خرجه مسلم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The separate report that a prophet drew lines and that a matching line is accurate is also said here to be unsound.
rows.anchor: كان نبي من الأنبياء يخط فمن وافق خطه فذاك

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi reports one view that line divination is permitted because a prophet practiced it, and another that it is forbidden because its prophetic method cannot be identified.
rows.anchor: جاء لإباحة الضرب لأن بعض الأنبياء كان يفعله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi adopts the prohibition: line divination derives guesses from planetary figures, claims inaccessible unseen knowledge, and seeking it is sinful or unbelief according to intent.
rows.anchor: ترجع إلى صور الكواكب، فيدل ما يخرج منها على ما تدل عليه تلك الكواكب

rows.speaker: الخطابي
rows.claim: Al-Khattabi reads the matching-line hadith as a warning: line reading was a prophetic sign whose practice ended with that prophet.
rows.anchor: قوله عليه السلام: «فمن وافق خطه فذاك»

rows.speaker: القاضي عياض
rows.claim: Qadi Iyad says the wording appears to affirm the successful match, but coincidence cannot be known and the law forbids divination and claims to the unseen; it grants no permission.
rows.anchor: لكن من أين تعلم الموافقة والشرع منع من التخرص وادعاء الغيب جملة

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Makki says the prophet who drew lines used his index and middle fingers in sand and then performed divination.
rows.anchor: وحكى مكي في تفسير قوله: «كان نبي من الأنبياء يخط» أنه كان يخط بأصبعه السبابة والوسطى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas describes a geomancer paid to draw quick lines in soft earth, erase them two at a time, and infer success from two remaining or failure from one; Arabs called it al-asham.
rows.anchor: هو الخط الذي يخطه الحازي فيعطى حلوانا فيقول: اقعد حتى أخط لك

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi allows dreams as a sign of the unseen because they are part of prophethood, and permits good-omen interpretation while prohibiting omens and divinatory augury.
rows.anchor: إن الله تعالى لم يبق من الأسباب الدالة على الغيب التي أذن في التعلق بها والاستدلال منها إلا الرؤيا فإنه أذن فيها

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Faʾl is taking encouragement from good words heard about a planned matter; one should proceed happily, while ignoring unpleasant words rather than turning back.
rows.anchor: والفأل: هو الاستدلال بما يسمع من الكلام على ما يريد من الأمر إذا كان حسنا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet prayed that there is no omen except God's omen, no good except God's good, and no deity besides Him.
rows.anchor: اللهم لا طير إلا طيرك ولا خير إلا خيرك ولا إله غيرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi accepts the poet's condemnation of divination and soothsaying but rejects including faʾl, which the law expressly exempts and commends.
rows.anchor: وهذا كلام صحيح، إلا في الفأل فإن الشرع استثناه وأمر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone knows the unseen except where He informs someone or gives a customary sign; such signs are defeasible, as date-palm flowering may fail or fruit may grow again after apparent loss.
rows.anchor: أن الله سبحانه منفرد بعلم الغيب، وأن أحدا لا يعلم ذلك إلا ما أعلمه الله

rows.speaker: ابن خويز منداد
rows.claim: Ibn Khuwayz Mindad says athārah means handwriting and reports that Malik initially ruled by handwriting when the writer was recognized.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { أو أثارة من علم } يريد الخط. وقد كان مالك رحمه الله يحكم بالخط

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik later reversed judgment by handwriting after fraud and forgery spread, saying that people's corruption brings new rulings.
rows.anchor: ثم رجع عن ذلك حين ظهر في الناس ما ظهر من الحيل والتزوير.

rows.speaker: ابن خويز منداد
rows.claim: Ibn Khuwayz says Malik's school permits judgment when witnesses authenticate a judge's letter or a will as handwriting even if they do not know its contents, and likewise a person's written admission of debt.
rows.anchor: فأما إذا شهد الشهود على الخط المحكوم به مثل أن يشهدوا أن هذا خط الحاكم وكتابه،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والكلبي وأبو بكر بن عياش
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Kalbi, Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, and others interpret athārah as a remnant of knowledge, as do the lexicons.
rows.anchor: وقيل: «أو أثارة من علم» أو بقية من علم قاله ابن عباس والكلبي وأبو بكر بن عياش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Athārah and atharah can mean a remaining portion, as in camels fattening on leftover fat; al-Raʿi's verse illustrates the usage.
rows.anchor: سمنت الإبل على أثارة أي بقية شحم كان قبل ذلك.

rows.speaker: ميمون بن مهران وأبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن وقتادة
rows.claim: Maimun ibn Mihran, Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman, and Qatada take athārah to mean a special portion of knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقال ميمون بن مهران وأبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن وقتادة: «أو أثارة من علم» خاصة من علم.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets it as a report transmitted from people who came before.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: رواية تأثرونها عمن كان قبلكم.

rows.speaker: عكرمة ومقاتل
rows.claim: Ikrima and Muqatil understand it as a report passed down from prophets.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة ومقاتل: رواية عن الأنبياء.

rows.speaker: القرظي
rows.claim: Al-Qurazi says it means an isnad, or chain of transmission.
rows.anchor: وقال القرظي: هو الإسناد.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads it as something that is brought forth or extracted.
rows.anchor: الحسن: المعنى شيء يثار أو يستخرج.

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says athārah means a sign; it is a verbal noun like generosity or bravery, from the root for a trace or transmitted report.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: «أو أثارة» أي علامة. والأثارة مصدر كالسماحة والشجاعة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Athar, athārah, and atharah can mean relating a report from someone else; a maʾthūr hadith is transmitted generation to generation with a sound chain.
rows.anchor: ومنه قيل: حديث مأثور أي نقله خلف عن سلف.

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Aʿsha's line about what is clear to the listener and transmitter is cited as evidence for the sense of transmitted report.
rows.anchor:
قال الأعشى: إن الذي فيه تماريتما
بين للسامع والآثر

rows.speaker: قراءة
rows.claim: A reading has u as the vowel of the hamza and a silent thāʾ in athrah; it can mean a remainder of knowledge or something inherited from earlier books.
rows.anchor: «أو أثرة» بضم الهمزة وسكون الثاء.

rows.speaker: السلمي والحسن وأبو رجاء
rows.claim: Al-Sulami, al-Hasan, and Abu Raja read atharah with a fatḥah on hamza and thāʾ, without the alif, meaning special knowledge granted or preferred to its holders.
rows.anchor: وقرأ السلمي والحسن وأبو رجاء بفتح الهمزة والثاء من غير ألف

rows.speaker: الحسن وعكرمة
rows.claim: Another report gives al-Hasan's reading atharah with open hamza and silent thāʾ; Ikrima explains it as an inheritance of knowledge.
rows.anchor: وروي عن الحسن أيضا وطائفة «أثرة» مفتوحة الألف ساكنة الثاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse lays out the forms of proof: rational argument that inert idols neither harm nor benefit, then transmitted proof from an earlier book or inherited knowledge.
rows.anchor: فيه بيان مسالك الأدلة بأسرها فأولها المعقول،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited word ṣawāb in the Day of Resurrection verse means the testimony that there is no god but God.
rows.anchor: يعني قول: لا إله إلا الله.

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj interprets Q as meaning that the matter has been decreed, parallel to his interpretation of Ḥā Mīm.
rows.anchor: أي قضي الأمر، كما قيل في «حم» أي حم الأمر.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas gives two interpretations: Q is a divine name by which God swears, and it is also a name of the Qur'an, as Qatada says.
rows.anchor: «ق» اسم من أسماء الله تعالى أقسم به. وعنه أيضا: أنه اسم من أسماء القرآن. وهو قول قتادة.

rows.speaker: القرظي
rows.claim: Al-Qurazi reads Q as the initials of divine names: Qadir, Qahir, Qarib, Qadi, and Qabid.
rows.anchor: وقال القرظي: افتتاح أسماء الله تعالى قدير وقاهر وقريب وقاض وقابض.

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says Q is the opening of the surah.
rows.anchor: فاتحة السورة. وقال أبو بكر

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
rows.claim: Abu Bakr al-Warraq reads it as an instruction to stay within God's commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الوراق: معناه قف عند أمرنا ونهينا ولا تعدهما.

rows.speaker: محمد بن عاصم الأنطاكي
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Asim al-Antaki interprets Q as God's nearness to His servants and cites the jugular-vein verse.
rows.anchor: هو قرب الله من عباده، بيانه { ونحن أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد }

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAta says God swears by the strength of Muhammad's heart, which bore the revelation without being affected because of his exalted state.
rows.anchor: أقسم الله بقوة قلب حبيبه محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، حيث حمل الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Majid means elevated in rank; al-Hasan also glosses it as noble.
rows.anchor: أي الرفيع القدر. وقيل: الكريم قاله الحسن.

rows.speaker: ابن بحر
rows.claim: Ibn Bahr says majid means abundant in worth and stature, not in number, illustrated by a proverb that two tree species yield exceptional fire.
rows.anchor: فزادا على سائر الشجر قاله ابن بحر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed oath answer is the statement that God knows what the earth diminishes from the dead, with an understood emphatic la- before it.
rows.anchor: على إرادة اللام أي لقد علمنا.

rows.speaker: الترمذي محمد بن علي
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi Muhammad ibn Ali chooses in-that-is-a-reminder as the oath's answer: God swears by power and the majestic Qur'an, whose account of creation and the afterlife reminds receptive hearts.
rows.anchor: وهو اختيار الترمذي محمد بن علي قال: «ق» قسم باسم هو أعظم الأسماء التي خرجت إلى العباد

rows.speaker: ابن كيسان
rows.claim: Ibn Kaysan identifies the oath's answer as the statement that not a word is uttered without a watcher.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان: جوابه { ما يلفظ من قول }.

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة
rows.claim: The Kufans take the oath's answer to be the statement that the disbelievers marveled.
rows.anchor: وقال أهل الكوفة: جواب هذا القسم { بل عجبوا }

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says the answer is omitted: the oath means that they will surely be resurrected, as the following question about becoming dust indicates.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش: جوابه محذوف كأنه قال: { ق والقرآن المجيد } لتبعثن يدل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative an is causal, meaning they marveled because a warner from among them came; the warner is Muhammad, and the pronoun can refer to disbelievers or to believers and disbelievers together.
rows.anchor: «أن» في موضع نصب على تقدير لأن جاءهم منذر منهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording shifts from the shared group to “the disbelievers” rather than “they said,” condemning their state and conduct.
rows.anchor: ثم ميز بينهم بقوله تعالى: { فقال الكافرون } ولم يقل فقالوا، بل قبح حالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAjīb is something wondrous; ʿujāb is another form, while the intensive ʿujjāb is stronger, along with uʿjūbah.
rows.anchor: العجيب الأمر الذي يتعجب منه، وكذلك العجاب بالضم، والعجاب بالتشديد أكثر منه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says their amazement was that they were called to worship one God; another view says they marveled at the warning of resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: عجبهم أن دعوا إلى إله واحد. وقيل: من إنذارهم بالبعث والنشور.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi gives priority to the explanation stated explicitly in the Qur'an: their wonder was that a warner came from among them.
rows.anchor: والذي نص عليه القرآن أولى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers' question has an omitted predicate: will we be raised after dying and becoming dust?
rows.anchor: { أإذا متنا وكنا ترابا } نبعث ففيه إضمار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rajaʿ means return; they call resurrection a remote return, meaning impossible.
rows.anchor: الرجع الرد أي هو رد بعيد أي محال.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second ellipsis supplies their repeated objection: they said, “Will we be resurrected when we die?”
rows.anchor: وفيه إضمار آخر أي وقالوا أنبعث إذا متنا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resurrection need not have been mentioned immediately before: it occurs elsewhere, the Qur'an is like one surah, and a warner's warning entails afterlife punishment and judgment.
rows.anchor: وذكر البعث وإن لم يجر هاهنا فقد جرى في مواضع، والقرآن كالسورة الواحدة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth consumes parts of their bodies, but nothing is lost from God's knowledge, so restoration cannot be frustrated.
rows.anchor: أي ما تأكل من أجسادهم فلا يضل عنا شيء حتى تتعذر علينا الإعادة.

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet warned Abdullah that he might live among a people whose covenants and trusts are corrupted and who differ among themselves; he interlaced his fingers. Abu Dawud transmitted it, and al-Qurtubi says he included it in al-Tadhkira.
rows.anchor: كيف بك يا عبد الله إذا كنت في قوم قد مرجت عهودهم وأماناتهم واختلفوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited verse describes tall, fruitful palms; the accompanying poetry says their height kept the harvest beyond reapers' hands.
rows.anchor: كرام في السماء ذهبن طولا وفات ثمارها أيدي الجناة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb basaqu means to rise above companions; absqat a she-camel means milk appeared in its udder before she gave birth, with related forms for such camels.
rows.anchor: ويقال: بسق فلان على أصحابه أي علاهم، وأبسقت الناقة إذا وقع في ضرعها اللبن

rows.speaker: قطبة بن مالك
rows.claim: Qutba ibn Malik is reported to have heard the Prophet read baṣiqāt with ṣād, but al-Qurtubi cites Muslim's report that Qutba repeated the word without knowing what the Prophet said and rejects changing sin to ṣād because of qaf.
rows.anchor: قال قطبة بن مالك: سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ «باصقات» بالصاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭalʿ is the first date fruit to emerge; the palm has produced it while it is still enclosed in its sheath before opening.
rows.anchor: الطلع هو أول ما يخرج من ثمر النخل يقال: طلع الطلع طلوعا وأطلعت النخلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nadīd means stacked or layered on one another; al-Bukhari defines it as the date cluster while still inside its sheath, not after it emerges.
rows.anchor: «نضيد» أي متراكب قد نضد بعضه على بعض. وفي البخاري: «النضيد» الكفرى مادام في أكمامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rizqan can be an object with an implied “We provided,” a complement of the planting understood as provision, or a purpose expression; provision is what is made ready for use.
rows.anchor: أي رزقناهم رزقا، أو على معنى أنبتناها رزقا لأن الإنبات في معنى الرزق،

words: وَأَحْيَيْنَا بِهِۦ بَلْدَةًۭ مَّيْتًۭا كَذَٰلِكَ ٱلْخُرُوجُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As God revives dead land by rain, He will bring people alive from their graves; the resurrection is likened to the land's revival.
rows.anchor: أي من القبور أي كما أحيا الله هذه الأرض الميتة فكذلك يخرجكم أحياء بعد موتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kāf in kathālika is in the predicate position of an initial clause; maytan is masculine because the intended referent is the place, though maytatan would also be valid.
rows.anchor: فالكاف في محل رفع على الابتداء. وقد مضى هذا المعنى في غير موضع. وقال «ميتا» لأن المقصود المكان ولو قال ميتة لجاز.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A woman described as muwaqqarah with a fatḥah on qaf is carrying a heavy load; a palm is muwaqqarah when its crop is abundant.
rows.anchor: وهذه امرأة موقرة بفتح القاف إذا حملت حملا ثقيلا. وأوقرت النخلة كثر حملها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The palm-tree form muwaqqir with a kasrah follows the pattern of ḥāmil for a woman, since bearing fruit is likened to pregnancy; the fatḥah form is irregular, and muwaqqar is also reported contrary to the usual pattern.
rows.anchor: وإنما قيل: موقر بكسر القاف على قياس قولك امرأة حامل، لأن حمل الشجر مشبه بحمل النساء فأما موقر بالفتح فشاذ،

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labid's line about palms carrying fruit is cited for the form muwaqqar; its plural is mawāqir.
rows.anchor:
عصب كوارع في خليج محلم
حملت فمنها موقر مكموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waqr with fatḥah means heaviness in the ear or deafness; waqirat udhُنuhu means his ear became deaf, with an unusual sukūn in the verbal noun.
rows.anchor: فأما الوقر بالفتح فهو ثقل الأذن، وقد وقرت أذنه توقر وقرا أي صمت،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The flowing things are ships driven easily by winds to wherever they are directed.
rows.anchor: السفن تجري بالرياح يسرا إلى حيث سيرت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative identifies the flowing things as clouds, which God directs across regions and lands.
rows.anchor: وقيل: السحاب وفي جريها يسرا على هذا القول وجهان: أحدهما إلى حيث يسيرها الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the cloud interpretation, yusran can mean ease of movement, a familiar usage among Arabs.
rows.anchor: الثاني هو سهولة تسييرها وذلك معروف عند العرب، كما قال الأعشى:

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Aʿsha compares a woman's easy-paced walk to a cloud's movement, neither slow nor rushed.
rows.anchor:
كما قال الأعشى:
كأن مشيتها من بيت جارتها
مشي السحابة لا ريث ولا عجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose-lām is connected to the meaning of God's ownership: He guides and misguides whom He wills in order to repay wrongdoers and reward the good.
rows.anchor: اللام متعلقة بالمعنى الذي دل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis treats God's ownership clause as parenthetic, leaving the sense that the Lord knows who strays and who is guided in order to repay them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: { ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض } معترض في الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third analysis makes the lām one of consequence: creation's ultimate outcome divides it into wrongdoers destined for Hell and good-doers destined for Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي لام العاقبة، أي ولله ما في السموات وما في الأرض أي وعاقبة أمر الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who avoid major sins and indecencies describe the people who do good.
rows.anchor: هذا نعت للمحسنين أي هم لا يرتكبون كبائر الإثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi identifies the greatest sin, shirk, as the intended major sin.
rows.anchor: وهو الشرك لأنه أكبر الآثام

rows.speaker: الأعمش ويحيى بن وثاب وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash, Yahya ibn Waththab, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi read the singular kabīr; Ibn Abbas explains that form as shirk.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش ويحيى بن وثاب وحمزة والكسائي «كبير» على التوحيد وفسره ابن عباس بالشرك.

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says major sins are any sins whose punishment ends in the Fire, while indecencies are any sins carrying a prescribed legal penalty.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: { كبائر الإثم } كل ذنب ختم بالنار. { والفواحش } كل ذنب فيه الحد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi also identifies indecencies with zina.
rows.anchor: { والفواحش } الزنى: وقال مقاتل: { كبائر الإثم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception of lamam is disconnected and refers to minor sins, which no one avoids completely except those God protects.
rows.anchor: ثم استثنى استثناء منقطعا وهي: المسألة الثانية: فقال: { إلا اللمم } وهي الصغائر

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة وابن عباس والشعبي
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra, Ibn Abbas, and al-Shaʿbi interpret lamam as everything short of zina.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو هريرة وابن عباس والشعبي: «اللمم» كل ما دون الزنى.

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
rows.claim: Muqatil ibn Sulayman reports the occasion: date-seller Nibhan lured a customer into his shop and solicited her; she refused, and he confessed to the Prophet, who asked whether her husband might be away campaigning; the verse then came down.
rows.anchor: وذكر مقاتل بن سليمان: " أن هذه الآية نزلت في رجل كان يسمى نبهان التمار

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبو سعيد الخدري وحذيفة ومسروق
rows.claim: Ibn Masud, Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, Hudhayfa, and Masruq say lamam is what falls short of intercourse: kissing, touching, looking, or lying together.
rows.anchor: وكذا قال ابن مسعود وأبو سعيد الخدري وحذيفة ومسروق: إن اللمم ما دون الوطء

rows.speaker: مسروق عن عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Masruq transmits Ibn Masud's account that the eyes' zina is looking, the hands' is touching, and the feet's is walking; the genitals confirm or disprove it, making it full zina if consummated and lamam otherwise.
rows.anchor: وروى مسروق عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: زنى العينين النظر، وزنى اليدين البطش

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن النبي
rows.claim: In Bukhari and Muslim, Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet's teaching that each person inevitably has a share of zina: the eyes look, the tongue speaks, the soul desires, and the genitals confirm or deny it.
rows.anchor: وفي صحيح البخاري ومسلم عن ابن عباس قال: ما رأيت شيئا أشبه باللمم مما قال أبو هريرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The complete, punishable zina is the act of the genitals; other bodily parts have their own share of sin.
rows.anchor: والمعنى: أن الفاحشة العظيمة والزنى التام الموجب للحد في الدنيا والعقوبة في الآخرة هو في الفرج

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن أبي هريرة عن النبي
rows.claim: A Muslim report adds that the ears' zina is listening, the heart desires, and the other limbs' zina is speech, touch, or walking, with the genitals confirming or denying it.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية أبي صالح عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

rows.speaker: طاووس عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Thaʿlabi cites a report from Tawus from Ibn Abbas that adds the lips' zina as kissing.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر الثعلبي حديث طاوس عن ابن عباس فذكر فيه الأذن واليد والرجل، وزاد فيه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another interpretation from Ibn Abbas is a person who slips into a sin and then repents; he cites the verse about God forgiving abundantly.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس أيضا: هو الرجل يلم بذنب ثم يتوب.

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas calls the Ibn Abbas interpretation of a sin followed by repentance the soundest and best-attested view.
rows.anchor: قال النحاس: هذا أصح ما قيل فيه وأجلها إسنادا.

rows.speaker: مجاهد والحسن والزهري
rows.claim: Mujahid, al-Hasan, and al-Zuhri say lamam is a sin committed once and not repeated; al-Zuhri gives zina, theft, and drinking wine followed by repentance as examples.
rows.anchor: عن الزهري، قال: اللمم أن يزني ثم يتوب فلا يعود، وأن يسرق أو يشرب الخمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse about remembering God, seeking forgiveness after wrongdoing, and not persisting in sin supports the view that lamam is a sin followed by repentance.
rows.anchor: والذين إذا فعلوا فاحشة أو ظلموا أنفسهم ذكروا الله فاستغفروا لذنوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following verse promises forgiveness, paralleling the statement after lamam that the Lord is vast in forgiveness.
rows.anchor:
أولئك جزآؤهم مغفرة من ربهم
[آل عمران: 136] فضمن لهم المغفرة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
rows.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As says lamam means anything short of shirk.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص: اللمم ما دون الشرك.

rows.speaker: ابن زيد وعكرمة والضحاك وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd, Ikrima, al-Dahhak, and Qatada define lamam as a sin with no worldly hadd and no threatened afterlife punishment, expiated by the five daily prayers; al-Awfi and al-Hakam transmit this from Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن زيد وعكرمة والضحاك وقتادة. ورواه العوفي والحكم بن عتيبة عن ابن عباس.

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi gives two senses: a minor sin with no hadd or afterlife threat, expiated by the five prayers while short of major sins, or a grave sin repeatedly committed and then repented from.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: اللمم على وجهين: كل ذنب لم يذكر الله عليه حدا في الدنيا ولا عذابا في الآخرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو هريرة وزيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurayra, and Zayd ibn Thabit say lamam means deeds from before Islam, which are not charged against converts; polytheists taunted Muslims that they had done such things before, prompting the verse. Zayd ibn Aslam and his son agree.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا وأبي هريرة وزيد بن ثابت: هو ما سلف في الجاهلية فلا يؤاخذهم به.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pre-Islam interpretation is compared with the rule allowing what preceded the prohibition on marrying two sisters to stand.
rows.anchor:
وهو كقوله تعالى:
وأن تجمعوا بين الأختين إلا ما قد سلف
[النساء: 23].

rows.speaker: نفطويه
rows.claim: Niftawayh says lamam is an occasional rather than habitual sin, since Arabs say someone visits only now and then; he rejects mere intention without action because the phrase for visiting requires that one actually came.
rows.anchor: وقيل: اللمم هو أن يأتي بذنب لم يكن له بعادة قاله نفطويه.

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ rejects interpreting lamam as merely intending without acting, since the Arabic phrase “he visited us” describes an act rather than an unfulfilled intention.
rows.anchor: قال: ولا يكون أن يلم ولا يفعل، لأن العرب لا تقول ألم بنا إلا إذا فعل الإنسان

rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Jawhari defines lamam as minor sins and also records the sense of approaching a sin without committing it.
rows.anchor: وفي الصحاح: وألم الرجل من اللمم وهو صغائر الذنوب، ويقال: هو مقاربة المعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed verse using alimmam before the caravan departs is cited to illustrate the sense of drawing near.
rows.anchor:
وأنشد غير الجوهري:
بزينب ألمم قبل أن يرحل الركب

rows.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
rows.claim: Ata ibn Abi Rabah says lamam is a habit of the self that occurs from time to time.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء بن أبي رباح: اللمم عادة النفس الحين بعد الحين.

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib says lamam is what merely crosses the heart.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن المسيب: هو ما ألم على القلب أي خطر.

rows.speaker: محمد بن الحنفية
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya says anything one intends, good or bad, is lamam, supported by the report that Satan and the angel each have a prompting.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن الحنفية: كل ما هممت به من خير أو شر فهو لمم.

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A prophetic report says that Satan has a prompting and the angel has a prompting.
rows.anchor: إن للشيطان لمة وللملك لمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi notes that he discussed the prompting report under the verse about Satan promising poverty in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor:
وقد مضى في «البقرة» عند قوله تعالى:
الشيطان يعدكم الفقر
[البقرة: 286].

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the root implies something done repeatedly but briefly, without deep involvement or persistence; it can mean visiting now and then, and hence a passing apparition of a dream.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق الزجاج: أصل اللمم والإلمام ما يعمله الإنسان المرة بعد المرة ولا يتعمق فيه ولا يقيم عليه

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Aʿsha's line about a vision of Qutayla briefly visiting illustrates the sense of ilmam.
rows.anchor:
قال الأعشى:
ألم خيال من قتيلة بعدما
وهى حبلها من حبلنا فتصرما

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Some take illa to mean “and,” but al-Farraʾ rejects this and construes lamam as sins approaching the category of minor offenses.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إلا بمعنى الواو. وأنكر هذا الفراء وقال: المعنى إلا المتقارب من صغار الذنوب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi rejects lamam as a merely accidental glance: such a glance is excused from the outset because it occurs without intent or choice.
rows.anchor: وقيل: اللمم النظرة التي تكون فجأة. قلت: هذا فيه بعد إذ هو معفو عنه ابتداء غير مؤاخذ به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lamam can also mean a touch of madness, a person afflicted with it, or a slight touch from jinn; a verse compares it to a dreamer's imagined word.
rows.anchor: واللمم أيضا طرف من الجنون، ورجل ملموم أي به لمم.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God's forgiveness is vast for anyone who repents of sin and seeks forgiveness.
rows.anchor: لمن تاب من ذنبه واستغفر قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: أبو ميسرة عمرو بن شرحبيل
rows.claim: Abu Maysara dreamed of domes in Paradise for Dhu al-Kala and Hawshab, who had killed one another; he was told they met God and found Him vast in forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو ميسرة عمرو بن شرحبيل وكان من أفاضل أصحاب ابن مسعود: رأيت في المنام كأني دخلت الجنة فإذا قباب مضروبة

rows.speaker: أبو خالد
rows.claim: Abu Khalid says he heard that Dhu al-Kala freed twelve thousand girls.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو خالد: بلغني أن ذا الكلاع أعتق اثني عشر ألف بنت.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows people better than they know themselves; “He created you from the earth” refers to their father Adam, created from clay, though the wording addresses descendants in the plural.
rows.anchor: يعني أباكم آدم من الطين وخرج اللفظ على الجمع

rows.speaker: الترمذي أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi Abu Abdullah rejects an Adam-only reading: creation happened in the shared soil raised from earth, from which waters and essences entered loins and were later extracted in differing forms, colors, and degrees of brightness.
rows.anchor: الترمذي أبو عبد الله: وليس هو كذلك عندنا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report says the first and later generations were shown before the Prophet's room, including those still in men's loins and mothers' wombs, represented in clay; he recognized them as Adam had learned the names.
rows.anchor: عرض علي الأولون والآخرون بين يدي حجرتي هذه الليلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi recalls the statement at the opening of al-Anʿam that each person is created from the soil of the place where he will be buried.
rows.anchor: قلت: وقد تقدم في أول «الأنعام» أن كل إنسان يخلق من طين البقعة التي يدفن فيها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajnna is the plural of janin, a child while in the womb; the name derives from being concealed and covered.
rows.anchor: جمع جنين وهو الولد ما دام في البطن، سمي جنينا لاجتنانه واستتاره.

rows.speaker: عمرو بن كلثوم
rows.claim: Amr ibn Kulthum's verse describing a child not yet known as a fetus is cited as linguistic evidence for janin.
rows.anchor:
قال عمرو بن كلثوم:
هجان اللون لم تقرأ جنينا

rows.speaker: مكحول
rows.claim: Mak-hul reflects that people survive successive stages—fetus, infant, youth, and elder—while many die at each stage, asking what remains to await in old age.
rows.anchor: وقال مكحول: كنا أجنة في بطون أمهاتنا فسقط منا من سقط وكنا فيمن بقي

rows.speaker: ثابت بن الحارث الأنصاري عن النبي
rows.claim: Thabit ibn al-Harith reports that Jews called a dead infant a ṣiddiq; the Prophet said they lied, since every soul created in the womb is destined either blessed or wretched, and this verse was revealed. A similar report comes from Aisha.
rows.anchor:
وروى ابن لهيعة عن الحرث بن يزيد عن ثابت بن الحرث الأنصاري قال:
" كانت اليهود تقول إذا هلك لهم صبي صغير: هو صديق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not praise or commend yourselves: this keeps one farther from ostentation and nearer to humility.
rows.anchor:
فلا تزكوا أنفسكم
[النجم: 32] أي لا تمدحوها ولا تثنوا عليها

rows.speaker: الحسن وغيره
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and others explain the one who is mindful as one who makes deeds sincere and fears God's punishment; God knows each soul's deeds and final destination.
rows.anchor: أي أخلص العمل واتقى عقوبة الله عن الحسن وغيره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi refers readers to the discussion of self-purification at the verse about people who praise themselves in al-Nisaʾ.
rows.anchor: وقد مضى في «النساء» الكلام في معنى هذه الآية عند قوله تعالى: { ألم تر إلى الذين يزكون أنفسهم }

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says he would declare no one in this community purified except the Messenger of God.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: ما من أحد من هذه الأمة أزكيه غير رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم.
